He is calmer and more honest with himself, but his first instinct is still to put Jeremiah before his own happiness. When Belly and Jeremiah announce their engagement, Conrad does not try to ruin it. He helps Belly with the wedding instead. He runs errands, fixes problems and pays attention when Jeremiah does not. The peach scene makes his feelings painfully obvious. Conrad notices Belly wants another peach, buys it for her and wipes the juice from her chin. He still struggles to say “I love you,” but his attention says it for him. We later learn that Conrad promised Susannah he would look after Jeremiah. He has spent years treating that promise as a rule that Jeremiah’s happiness must always come before his own. Learning what happened in Cabo finally changes that. Conrad admits that he still loves Belly, although his timing remains painfully Conrad: the wedding is almost there. The wedding does not collapse because of his confession alone. Belly and Jeremiah’s engagement is already carrying betrayal, secrets and Belly’s unresolved feelings for Conrad. When Belly admits that she still loves him, Jeremiah refuses to marry her. What Conrad does next proves that he has changed. He works on repairing his relationship with Jeremiah. He writes to Belly without demanding an answer. Then he goes to Paris and tells her how he feels without hiding behind another sacrifice. Belly initially sends him away, and Conrad respects her decision. She is the one who runs to the train and chooses him. For once, Conrad does not decide what is best for her. He lets Belly decide for herself. And that is the biggest clue for the movie. The movie is now in production, and Jenny Han has said it will follow another major milestone in Belly’s life. Since Belly and Conrad are together and their wedding has not yet appeared on screen, the milestone is very likely their marriage. I do not think the movie will reopen the love triangle. Belly had an entire life in Paris before choosing Conrad freely. Making her question that choice again would undo the ending of season three. What feels more believable is that the movie will show Belly and Conrad trying to build a real adult life together. Belly has created a future beyond Cousins, while Conrad’s medical path has taken him to California. They will have to decide where to live and how to support both careers. Conrad’s old response would be to sacrifice his own future, tell Belly she deserves better and quietly leave. His growth will be learning to make that decision with her instead. The wedding could also bring Conrad’s grief back. Susannah imagined Belly becoming part of the Fisher family, but she will not be there to see it happen. Conrad may panic or pull away when that loss becomes real again. The difference this time should be simple: he tells Belly, Jeremiah or Steven that he is struggling, accepts their help and stays. Jeremiah also needs to be part of the ending. Conrad has spent years believing that being a good brother means giving Jeremiah whatever he wants. The movie can finally show both brothers choosing each other without turning Belly into something one of them has won. Jeremiah standing beside Conrad at the wedding would complete that story better than another fight ever could. So this is what I think we will see: a Belly and Conrad wedding in Cousins, Susannah’s absence quietly felt, Jeremiah beside his brother and one final moment when Conrad is tempted to disappear but does not. When you and I are watching him reach for Belly’s hand, the ring will not be the detail I am waiting for. I will be watching to see whether Conrad finally understands that he does not have to leave to prove he loves someone. Your Conrad department has reached its verdict: this time, he stays.

posts.title: Belly Still Hasn’t Opened Susannah’s Letter
posts.subtitle: The unopened note may have less to do with which Fisher Belly marries and everything to do with whether she has finally lived enough to choose for herself.
posts.body: Susannah’s letter has already survived a knocked over tray, a switched envelope and a wedding that never happened. Yet Belly still has not broken the seal. That feels far too deliberate to be a forgotten detail. My theory is that the letter reached Belly on the correct day, but it reached the wrong version of her. If you need a quick refresh, Susannah writes the wedding letters in Season 2, Episode 8, shortly before her death. Laurel accidentally knocks the tray from her lap, scattering the letters and envelopes across the bed. Susannah puts everything back together, but Conrad’s letter ends up inside Jeremiah’s envelope. Belly finally receives her own letter in Season 3, Episode 8, “Last Kiss,” while she is waiting to marry Jeremiah. Laurel hands her the sealed envelope, but Belly says she does not think she can read it yet. Laurel takes it back. After the wedding is called off, the last confirmed person holding Belly’s letter is Laurel. And honestly, Belly’s hesitation makes complete sense. Jeremiah is missing, Conrad has confessed that he still loves her and Belly is trying to hold together a future that has started falling apart before she can even walk down the aisle. Opening a letter from Susannah in that moment would mean inviting one more powerful voice into a decision Belly is already struggling to make. Susannah had spent years imagining Belly ending up with one of her boys. Belly knew that. She had grown up inside Susannah’s picture of Cousins, infinity and the four children becoming one family forever. A wedding letter could easily feel like Susannah’s final instruction, especially to a girl who was still afraid that leaving Jeremiah also meant losing the Fishers, the beach house and the version of Susannah she carried with her. But the most interesting part is that Susannah’s letter in the final book does not actually choose Conrad or Jeremiah. Susannah pictures Belly “about thirty or so,” after a life filled with adventures and romances. She imagines her marrying a man who is steady, strong and kind. Then she adds that he may not even have the last name Fisher. That one detail changes the entire meaning of the letter. Susannah is not asking Belly to complete the future she once imagined for their families. She is telling her that she will always be Susannah’s girl, even if she leaves Cousins, loves other people and marries neither of her sons. The letter does not trap Belly inside Susannah’s dream. It gives her permission to outgrow it. The Belly standing in the bridal suite with Jeremiah is only twenty one. She is giving up Paris, fighting with Laurel, pushing Taylor away and rushing into a marriage partly because slowing down would force her to face everything she has been avoiding. She has not become the woman Susannah describes in the letter yet. She is still trying to preserve her childhood instead of choosing her adult life. That is why the book saving the letter for Belly’s wedding to Conrad carries a completely different meaning. By then, Belly has travelled, lived away from Cousins, had other experiences and returned because she wants to, not because she is scared of losing the Fishers. She is no longer waiting for Susannah to tell her which boy belongs in her future. The show has already taken Belly through its own version of that journey. She builds a life in Paris, begins calling herself Isabel and eventually chooses Conrad after learning that she can exist without either brother. If the film brings the unopened letter back before their wedding, I do not think its purpose will be to reveal that Susannah “always knew” they belonged together. Conrad and Belly have already made that decision themselves. Instead, Belly may finally read the description of the woman Susannah imagined and realise that she has become her. Conrad will matter because he is the man Belly chose after she had somewhere else to go, while Susannah’s line will prove that her love was never conditional on that choice. And I think that is the scene waiting inside this little envelope. Belly will hear Susannah’s voice again, but for once, she will not need it to tell her what to do. It was waiting for Belly to stop needing Susannah to choose for her.

posts.title: All Eight Harry Potter Movies Are Returning to Theaters
posts.subtitle: The entire saga is returning for one week, but Sorcerer’s Stone has the detail that makes this more than another anniversary screening.
posts.body: You can probably hear the opening music already. Twenty five years after Harry first walked into the Great Hall, all eight Harry Potter movies are returning to theaters worldwide. But only one film is bringing something fans have never seen before. Tickets go on sale: July 31, Harry Potter’s birthday Theater dates: August 27 through September 3 Movies returning: All eight Harry Potter films Exclusive addition: 12 minutes of unseen behind the scenes footage The only film receiving it: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone, also known as Philosopher’s Stone That final detail matters because the 12 minutes are not deleted scenes being restored to the film. No extended cut has been announced, so fans should not expect a missing Hogwarts class or a new scene that changes the original story. Instead, the bonus will take viewers behind the making of the first movie. Its exact contents have not been revealed yet, which makes those 12 minutes the most interesting part of the entire event. Sorcerer’s Stone is also the perfect film to receive them. It was the moment Hogwarts had to become real for the first time. The moving staircases, floating candles, Diagon Alley and the Great Hall all had to match a world that millions of readers had already imagined. Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint were also at the beginning of their careers. Seeing Harry, Ron and Hermione meet again on a theater screen is already nostalgic. Watching unseen footage from the production gives fans a glimpse of how that friendship and that world were first created. The other seven films will return in their familiar theatrical versions. Watching the complete series within one week would require nearly 20 hours in a theater, so attempting all eight is less of a casual rewatch and more of a temporary lifestyle choice. The timing has been carefully chosen too. Tickets arrive on Harry’s birthday, while the screening week includes September 1, the day Hogwarts students return to school. The anniversary is following the calendar of the story itself. With a new Harry Potter television adaptation also preparing to introduce Hogwarts to another generation, this rerelease feels like a quiet meeting between two eras. The new version is getting ready to begin, but the original films are receiving one more week on the big screen first. And that is why the 12 minutes matter. Nostalgia may make fans notice the rerelease, but unseen material gives them a reason to buy a ticket. Twenty five years ago, Sorcerer’s Stone showed us the magic. This time, it may finally show us a little more of how that magic was made.

posts.title: Chuck and Blair Were Never the Books’ Great Love Story
posts.subtitle: The show gave Blair’s first time and future to Chuck. The books had someone else in mind.
posts.body: Blair steps onto the stage at Victrola after everything with Nate falls apart. Chuck watches her dance, she looks completely free for once, and later they end up together in the back of his limo. If you have watched Gossip Girl, you know that moment. It changes the entire show. That night becomes the beginning of Chair. From there, Chuck and Blair spend years falling in love, hurting each other, breaking up, getting back together and acting like one honest conversation would physically kill them. Eventually, the show gives them a wedding and a son named Henry. Their story begins in a limo and ends as the biggest romance in the series. But the books tell a very different story. Chuck is not Blair’s great love there. He is not even one of the main characters at first. The emotional centre of the novels is Blair, Serena and Nate, whose friendship is tangled up in years of jealousy, betrayal and romantic confusion. Basically, Nate cannot decide which best friend he loves, and somehow both girls are left doing all the emotional work. Very Nate, honestly. And yes, here is the detail everyone wants to know. Blair loses her virginity to Nate in the books, not Chuck. She waits until the sixth novel, You’re the One That I Want. Blair has been planning that moment for ages. She wants it to be perfect, romantic and worthy of the old films she keeps replaying in her head. She buys condoms. Chooses the right clothes. She prepares for every possible detail. The only thing she cannot organise is Nate. Before Blair sleeps with him, Nate has already slept with Serena. In fact, Nate and Serena lost their virginities to each other before the first book even begins. Blair does not know this at first, which is why Serena’s return to Manhattan causes so much damage. Nate is Blair’s boyfriend, Serena is her best friend, and both of them are hiding the one secret that would hurt her most. The first novel is built around that betrayal. So when Blair finally sleeps with Nate, it is not simply a romantic milestone. It is tied to everything she wants from him: proof that he chooses her, proof that Serena is no longer between them and proof that the future Blair planned might still happen. Of course, this is Gossip Girl, so none of those proofs stay reliable for very long. Chuck is doing something completely different in the early books, and there is no easy way to soften it. He pins Serena down and kisses her against her will in his family’s hotel suite. Later, he corners Jenny in a bathroom stall at the Kiss on the Lips party and pulls down her dress before she locks herself away and calls Dan for help. These scenes position Chuck as a threat to the girls, not as Blair’s hidden soulmate. By the third book, even the publisher’s description has Blair and Serena plotting revenge on him. The television series did not originally plan to make Chuck and Blair a couple either. Chuck entered the show as a villain. Then Ed Westwick and Leighton Meester started sharing scenes, their chemistry worked immediately, and the story changed. Co creator Josh Schwartz said their scenes “crackled” and that the chemistry between them took over. Once the writers saw the limo scene, they knew the pairing had become something much bigger. It was a smart television decision. Chuck and Blair could match each other’s ambition, cruelty and love of scheming in a way that Blair and Nate never could. Nate often drifted through the books unsure of what he wanted. Chuck challenged Blair, which gave the show years of tension and some genuinely unforgettable scenes. But making Chuck a romantic lead also created a problem. The series wanted viewers to believe he had changed without always giving enough weight to the serious things he had done. His love for Blair became proof of his redemption, even when Blair was also the person most affected by his worst choices. The chemistry was real, but chemistry does not automatically erase consequences. The books eventually experiment with Chuck and Blair, but much later. After studying abroad and becoming calmer, Chuck dates Blair in the college sequel. He even surprises her with an apartment, while his mother begins talking about children. TV Blair spends years waiting for Chuck to commit. Book Blair receives commitment and decides everyone needs to slow down immediately. She breaks up with him because the relationship is moving too quickly. That short relationship does not replace the story the novels have been telling all along. The final emotional pull returns to Blair, Serena and Nate, before Blair and Serena finally choose their friendship over continuing the same exhausting triangle. Chuck was not the only character whose destination television changed. Still, it is easy to understand why Chair took over. Without Chuck and Blair, Gossip Girl would have been closer to the books, but it probably would not be the same show people are still arguing about today. That limo belongs to Chuck and Blair, but the books’ great love story never did. confidential note: Book Chuck has a pet monkey named Sweetie. He dresses her in little outfits and carries her around with him. The show later gives Chuck a dog named Monkey as a small nod to this very strange piece of book canon. milk mondays ruling: The show made the right choice by following Ed Westwick and Leighton Meester’s chemistry. Chair gave Gossip Girl its most memorable romance, but the writing sometimes rushed past behaviour that deserved more serious consequences. The books may have less epic romance, but they are clearer about who Chuck originally was. next on milk mondays: Jenny got an entire life after Manhattan that television never used. your ruling: Would the show still have become iconic without Chair?

posts.title: Did Max Deserve to Die in The Devil’s Mouth?
posts.subtitle: She chose the dangerous red path and kept ignoring Sara’s warnings, then admitted she was wrong only moments before the shark killed her.
posts.body: If you haven’t watched the movie yet, stay anyway. You love reading Milk Mondays, I love having you here, and we can both politely pretend there are absolutely no spoilers swimming below. Lana Condor and Gavin Casalegno in the same beach movie should have been a very safe little treat for anyone who still has Lara Jean and Jeremiah living in their head. Instead, Gavin’s Greg becomes shark food, while Lana’s Max spends most of the movie making choices that had me wanting to personally confiscate the cave map from her. The shark causes the actual bloodshed in The Devil’s Mouth, but Max and Sara’s friendship is what makes the ending interesting. Remove the cave, the flooding and the extremely committed bull shark, and their problem is painfully familiar: Max has become the friend who makes every decision, while Sara has become the friend who agrees because disagreeing feels harder. You know those friendships where one person books the table, chooses the holiday, speaks to the waiter and somehow also decides where both of you should live after graduation? Max is that friend. At first, it can look helpful. She is confident, organised and always ready with a plan. Slowly, you realise nobody is actually being asked, especially Sara. Every old friendship creates roles. Max is the brave one who takes charge. Sara is the cautious one who needs reassurance. Those roles probably helped them once, but Sara has outgrown hers and Max has not noticed. Sara also has a real reason for staying loyal. Max supported her after her father died, so their friendship is carrying years of love and gratitude. Sara behaves as though saying no to Max now would somehow erase everything Max did for her then. It would not, of course, but loyalty can feel strangely close to debt when someone helped you through the worst part of your life. The boat incident shows this before anyone reaches the cave. Sara goes swimming, the group leaves without noticing and she is badly stung by jellyfish. When they return, Max feels guilty, but she cannot simply sit with the fact that she hurt her friend. She becomes defensive, Sara comforts her, and somehow the person covered in jellyfish stings is also managing everyone else’s emotions. Gorgeous holiday. No notes. The next day, Max secretly pays Wat, their cave guide, to watch Sara more closely. She is trying to care for her, which is why their friendship is more complicated than “Max is awful.” The problem is that she never asks Sara whether she wants help. Max decides what Sara needs, arranges it privately and then feels hurt when Sara does not appreciate it. Overprotection can exist alongside genuine closeness, which is exactly why it can be hard to recognise. A controlling friend does not always look controlling. Sometimes she looks like the person who makes life easier for you, until you realise she is also speaking for you, choosing for you and treating your independence like a personal rejection. Then comes the red path. Wat explains that the green route is safer. The red route is longer and more dangerous, especially after the recent flooding. Sara wants green, but Max hears “dangerous and not recommended” as a personal invitation and talks everyone into choosing red. Max does not create the storm or place the shark inside the cave. Wat still agrees to guide them, and the rest of the group chooses to follow. Blaming every death entirely on Max would be too easy. What she does control is how many warnings she ignores after that first decision. Dead sea animals begin appearing inside the freshwater cave. Adrienne injures her leg. Wat wants to turn back, but Max insists on continuing because she does not want the experience to be wasted. Even after they discover that a bull shark is hunting inside the caves, Max keeps treating every disagreement like a vote she needs to win. That is the most frustrating thing about her. Max does not listen to find out whether Sara might be right. She listens for a pause where she can take charge again. Wat, Greg and Adrienne are killed. The group is shrinking, their options are disappearing and Sara is still the person carrying the useful supplies, reading the map and noticing what everyone else misses. Yet Max continues treating her like the nervous friend who needs to be managed. After the deaths, Sara studies Wat’s map and suggests using the tide to reach an opening connected to the ocean. Max rejects the plan and chooses a route through narrow underwater tunnels instead. Sara and James disagree, but Max starts leaving without them, knowing they will follow because separating feels even more dangerous. James becomes trapped between the rocks and eventually drowns after telling Sara and Max to leave him behind. When the women finally reach another air pocket, they discover that Max has led them in a complete circle. They are back near the place where Greg and Adrienne died. And honestly, that circle explains Max better than another dramatic speech ever could. She has spent the entire friendship believing that moving confidently means moving in the right direction. Sara has spent it believing that following Max is safer than trusting herself. Now they are both standing in the same place, except almost everyone they love is dead. Sara finally tells Max that her choices helped get them there. For once, Max has no plan, no clever reply and nobody left to convince. My read is that Max’s confidence was never as secure as it looked. Control is simply how she handles fear. If she can organise everything, she never has to admit that she feels helpless. If Sara needs her, she never has to wonder whether Sara might choose a different life without her. That is why Sara becoming capable feels threatening to Max, even though Max loves her. Sara is supposed to be the cautious sidekick. If Sara can read the map, create the escape plan and survive without being rescued, Max has to accept that their old friendship no longer works. Lana Condor explained that Max sees Sara as someone she will always have in her “back pocket,” rather than fully recognising her as a separate person. It is a harsh description, but it fits. Max includes Sara in every plan while rarely allowing Sara to shape one. Near the end, Max finally admits that she was wrong. She recognises Sara’s strength and agrees to follow her plan. The exchange was added shortly before filming because Max needed to truly see Sara before her death. Without it, the shark attack would feel like a punishment written for the irritating character. With it, Max dies just after becoming self aware enough to understand what she ruined. The movie then makes their friendship very literal. Sara ties herself to Max with a rope so she can help her injured friend climb toward an exit. When the shark grabs Max, Sara is dragged into the water too. The film is not exactly being subtle here, but it works. Sara has been pulled along by Max’s choices for the entire movie. Now she is physically attached to the consequences of one more decision. Sara still tries to save her. She cuts the rope only when holding on will kill them both. That is important because she is not abandoning Max out of anger. She is finally accepting that loving someone cannot require her to disappear with them. Once Sara is alone, she remembers what Wat said about the cave’s unstable rocks. She lures the shark into striking them until the structure collapses and kills it. The knowledge needed to survive was available earlier. Sara simply trusted Max’s judgment more than her own. So, did Max deserve to die? No. She deserved consequences, a very serious apology and a friendship where Sara was no longer expected to obey her. Being controlling and selfish does not make death a fair punishment. Still, I understand why her ending feels like karma. Max ignores Sara when the danger is small, ignores her when the danger becomes obvious and keeps ignoring her after people begin dying. By the time she finally listens, there is no safe path left for either of them. That is also what makes the ending sad. Max was not pretending to love Sara. She simply never learned how to love her without managing her. Max finally sees that Sara never needed another leader. She needed her best friend.

posts.title: Who Was The Summer I Turned Pretty’s Real Augustine?
posts.subtitle: Belly, Conrad and Jeremiah each match one part of Taylor Swift’s song, but the ending makes the final answer much simpler.
posts.body: It is August again, which means The Summer I Turned Pretty fans have returned to one of the fandom’s oldest arguments: who is the show’s real Augustine? Quick refresher if the folklore lore has left your brain. In Taylor Swift’s fictional love triangle, James is with Betty, spends one summer with Augustine and then returns to Betty. Augustine believed her relationship with James could become something lasting, but James’s heart was still tied to someone else. Taylor later explained that Augustine genuinely loved James and thought their relationship was real. So here is the easiest way to remember the three roles: James is the person caught between two loves. Betty is the old love James returns to. Augustine is the person who believed the new relationship would last, only to be left behind. Now, back to Cousins. The most popular comparison makes Belly James, Conrad Betty and Jeremiah Augustine. Fans were making that exact connection long before Season 3 aired. Belly chooses Jeremiah at the end of Season 2, stays with him through college and agrees to marry him. But after their engagement ends, she eventually finds her way back to Conrad. That already makes Jeremiah the obvious Augustine. Still, the comparison becomes confusing because all three characters relate to the song in different ways. Belly shares Augustine’s habit of believing that whatever feels right now must be forever. She spends years wanting Conrad and sees their relationship as the love story she has always waited for. When that falls apart, she becomes equally certain that Jeremiah is her future. Then the engagement ends, she leaves for Paris and tries to convince herself that Cousins belongs to a finished part of her life. Belly keeps changing her idea of forever because she is still learning what she actually wants. That makes her similar to Augustine emotionally, but it does not make her Augustine in the triangle. Belly is the person making the choices. Both brothers are waiting to find out where her heart will land. She chooses Conrad, then Jeremiah and finally Conrad again. That places Belly much closer to James, the person moving between two relationships. Conrad creates a more convincing argument. He spends the summer in Cousins helping Belly plan her wedding to Jeremiah while still loving her himself. He drives her to choose cakes, suggests using Susannah’s hydrangeas and convinces Laurel to attend the wedding. He is beside Belly constantly, but he cannot ask her to be with him. If we were choosing Augustine based only on emotion, Conrad would win. His entire summer is filled with small moments that mean far more to him than he can admit. He gets time with Belly, but no promise that she will ever be his again. The problem is that Augustine’s story does not end with James returning to her. James returns to Betty. Belly returns to Conrad. Jenny Han has said that Season 3 was built around Belly and Conrad finding their way back to each other. Their reunion was the destination of the season. Conrad may feel like Augustine while Belly is engaged, but he holds Betty’s place in the larger story. He is the first love Belly tries to leave behind and eventually chooses again. That leaves Jeremiah. The main argument against Jeremiah being Augustine is that his relationship with Belly was far more serious than Augustine’s summer with James. Belly and Jeremiah date for years. They share a college life, search for an apartment and plan a wedding. Nobody orders that much champagne for a casual fling. But the show does not copy the song scene for scene. Belly does not secretly spend one summer with Jeremiah before running back to Conrad. The comparison is about where each person stands when the triangle finally ends. Jeremiah believes Belly choosing him means she has finished loving Conrad. Their engagement is supposed to settle the question permanently. Yet Jeremiah never feels completely secure because he knows Conrad still matters to her. He knows Belly and Conrad secretly spent Christmas together. He sees how easily they understand each other. And when Conrad finally admits that he still loves Belly, Jeremiah asks her the question their entire relationship has been avoiding. Does part of her still love Conrad? Belly admits that it does. She tells Jeremiah she still chooses him, but he knows that is no longer enough. He cannot marry Belly while she is using their wedding to prove that Conrad no longer matters. They end the engagement because Belly cannot promise that her love for Conrad is gone. That is what makes Jeremiah the real Augustine. He believed the relationship he had with Belly was leading to forever. The relationship was real, and Belly truly loved him, but her love for Jeremiah never completely replaced what she felt for Conrad. The final mapping is much simpler than it first appears. Belly is James because she moves between two loves. Conrad is Betty because he is the love she returns to. Jeremiah is Augustine because he believed he was Belly’s final choice, then learned that her heart was still connected to someone who came before him. Jeremiah did not imagine Belly’s love. He only imagined that it had ended her love for Conrad.

posts.title: Jenny Humphrey Got Ten More Books After Leaving Manhattan
posts.subtitle: The show treated Jenny’s exit like a punishment, while the books turned Waverly Academy into the fresh start she had always wanted.
posts.body: Jenny Humphrey leaves Manhattan looking like someone whose story has reached its final page. Rufus sends her to Hudson, Blair tells her never to return, and Jenny agrees that staying away from the Upper East Side might be the only way she can stop becoming someone she no longer recognises. After that, television gives us updates instead of a real story. Jenny studies fashion in London and briefly returns in the finale carrying a bag marked “J for Waldorf,” which suggests she now has a fashion line connected to Blair’s company. It is a lovely little detail, but it only tells us where Jenny ends up. We never see how she gets there. The books answer that question with ten more novels. Book Jenny also leaves Constance Billard and her Manhattan past behind, but she does not disappear into someone else’s storyline. She moves to Waverly Academy, an elite boarding school in New York horse country, and becomes the centre of a new series called The It Girl. The spinoff begins with her arrival in 2005 and continues through ten full books, ending with Classic in 2010. So no, Jenny does not simply receive a few extra chapters after leaving Manhattan. She gets a new school, new friends, new rivals, new romances and enough trouble to keep an entire second franchise alive. Waverly works so well for Jenny because reinvention has always been the thing she wants most. In Manhattan, she is constantly introduced through other people. She is Dan’s little sister, the Brooklyn outsider, Blair’s latest project or the younger girl trying to enter Serena’s world. Even when Jenny becomes Queen, she is taking over a role that Blair created. At Waverly, nobody knows Little J. Jenny arrives determined to become a more confident and sophisticated version of herself. She has already named this imagined person “New Jenny” in her own mind before she has properly settled into her room. That is very Jenny. Give her one train ride and she will return with a complete new identity planned. Her roommates are Callie Vernon and Brett Messerschmidt, two of Waverly’s most popular girls. Jenny is placed in the bed that once belonged to their former roommate, Tinsley Carmichael, the school’s legendary It Girl who was expelled the year before. This sounds like the perfect opening for Jenny. The most powerful girl is gone, her place is empty and a completely unknown student has arrived from Manhattan to fill it. Jenny finally enters a social world where she is not automatically standing behind Blair or Serena. Of course, the fresh start begins going wrong almost immediately. Callie’s boyfriend, Easy Walsh, becomes interested in Jenny. He is soon discovered nearly naked in the girls’ room, and Jenny is pressured to accept the blame even though she was not responsible. She has barely unpacked and is already facing the Disciplinary Committee. Manhattan may be gone, but trouble has apparently forwarded its mail. Then Tinsley returns to Waverly in the second book. She arrives by seaplane, because apparently walking back into school would not make enough of a point. Tinsley finds Jenny sleeping in her old bed, living with her closest friends and receiving attention from the entire campus. Jenny has accidentally stepped into the exact life Tinsley expected to reclaim. That rivalry gives Jenny something television rarely allowed her to have: a social battle that belongs completely to her. Tinsley is not a replacement Blair. She has her own history with Callie and Brett, her own power at Waverly and a personal reason to see Jenny as a threat. Their relationship changes over the series as competition, betrayal and reluctant friendship keep pulling them together. Jenny also makes new mistakes. She becomes involved with Easy while his relationship with Callie is still a mess. She gets caught in rumours, romantic triangles and school scandals. At one point, she accepts responsibility for a barn fire she did not start and nearly loses her place at Waverly again. This is where the spinoff becomes more interesting than a simple fantasy about Jenny finally becoming popular. A new school cannot automatically create a new person. Jenny keeps bringing the same hunger with her: she wants to be admired, chosen and accepted so badly that she sometimes ignores what it will cost. But Waverly gives her room to face that without being pushed back into Blair’s shadow every time. Jenny builds friendships with girls who see her as an equal. She becomes important because of the choices she makes there, rather than because she has managed to enter an older girl’s party. She is still insecure and impulsive, but she is no longer waiting beside the main story for someone to notice her. The ten books also let Waverly grow beyond Jenny. Callie, Brett and Tinsley receive their own relationships, secrets and conflicts. Gossip spreads through emails and instant messages instead of posts from Manhattan’s anonymous narrator. By the time the series reaches its final book, Waverly feels like a complete social world rather than a temporary place where Jenny was sent away. That is the biggest difference between her two departures. Television removes Jenny from Manhattan so she can escape the damage the Upper East Side has done to her. The books understand that leaving is only half of a reinvention. The more interesting half is watching what she builds next, including all the mistakes she makes while trying. On television, Jenny closes the door and eventually returns as a successful designer whose missing years we have to imagine. In the books, she walks through that same door and finds ten novels waiting on the other side. Manhattan was never Jenny Humphrey’s ending. It was the place she had to leave before the story could finally call her the main character. milk mondays ruling: The books gave Jenny the stronger departure. Television showed us the successful designer she eventually became, but Waverly let us watch her earn that reinvention through new friendships, fresh mistakes and choices that finally belonged to her. Jenny did not need another chance to rule Manhattan. She needed a world where she could become important without Blair deciding whether she was allowed to stay. next on milk mondays: Television’s biggest final reveal belonged to Dan. His book version was never heading towards the same secret. your ruling: Would you rather have watched Jenny build J for Waldorf or watched her become Waverly’s new It Girl?

posts.title: Here Are All the Movies Lola Tung Is Starring in Next
posts.subtitle: Everything Lola has coming next, from a bloody horror film to a soccer romance.
posts.body:
Okay, so Lola Tung’s next few projects are actually a little wild.

Instead of choosing one predictable follow up, she currently has a small town dramedy, a horror movie, a completely secret film and what appears to be a sapphic soccer romance waiting for us. No new television show has been announced yet, so right now we are very much entering Lola Tung’s movie era.

Here is everything we know so far.

1. Chasing Summer

Chasing Summer follows Jamie, a disaster relief worker who loses her job and gets dumped by her boyfriend around the same time. She returns to the small Texas hometown she left years ago, moves back in with her parents and starts confronting the friends, relationships and embarrassing old memories she thought she had escaped.

Basically, everything in her life falls apart and then her hometown decides to make it worse. Cute.

Lola plays Harper, a younger woman Jamie meets while working at her sister’s roller rink. Harper becomes one of Jamie’s new friends as she tries to work out what exactly she is doing with her life.

Iliza Shlesinger leads the movie as Jamie, with Garrett Wareing, Cassidy Freeman, Tom Welling and Megan Mullally completing the principal cast alongside Lola. Aimee Garcia, Jeff Perry and David Castañeda are also part of the wider ensemble.

This is not a movie built entirely around Lola, but I’m kind of happy about that. It gives her the chance to be funny, relaxed and slightly chaotic without having to carry every emotional crisis herself. Sometimes the supporting character who walks into a mess with fresh eyes ends up being the person everyone likes most.

The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 26, 2026, before screening at SXSW in March and the Nantucket Film Festival in June. It still does not have a confirmed general release date or streaming home. So yes, technically several festival audiences have watched it. The rest of us are just sitting here waiting politely.

2. The Young People

And now we go from roller skating and hometown problems to Lola covered in blood. Normal career progression, obviously.

Lola and Nico Parker are leading The Young People, a new horror film written and directed by Osgood Perkins. Nicole Kidman, Tatiana Maslany, Heather Graham and Johnny Knoxville are also part of the cast, which is such a random and interesting group of people that I already need to know what happened on that set.

The cast is even bigger than that. Cush Jumbo, Brendan Hines, Lexi Minetree and Good One star Lily Collias have also joined the movie. Neon is releasing it theatrically in the United States, so this one is not being quietly dropped onto a streaming service without warning.

The story is still being kept secret. It has only been described as a coming of age “bad trip,” which tells us almost nothing while somehow making it sound worse.

The first look at Lola showed her covered in blood, but we do not know whose blood it is, what happened to her or whether her character is the person in danger. She could be the terrified girl trying to survive the movie. She could also be the reason everyone else needs to survive it. Both options work for me.

The movie has finished filming and was listed as being in post production in July 2026. Neon is still expected to release it theatrically sometime in 2026, but an exact date has not been announced. This feels a little rude considering they already showed us a blood covered Lola and then disappeared.

This might be the project that changes how people see her as an actress. Horror does not let someone stay charming and emotionally familiar for long. It asks them to become frightened, unsettling or completely impossible to read.

We have never seen Lola do anything like that before, and I really want to know whether we are supposed to trust her.

3. Please

Please is giving us almost nothing right now. A title, a cast and silence. Thank you so much, everyone involved.

Lola has joined Gracie Abrams, Tom Burke, Connor Storrie and David Jonsson in the film, which is being written and directed by Halina Reijn. Gracie is expected to lead the movie in her first acting role, while every character surrounding her, including Lola’s, is still being kept secret.

The full plot has not been announced, but A24 has finally given us three words: “sexy and romantic.” Halina has also said the story explores something women will recognise, while Gracie described the script as dark and twisty. Helpful? Slightly. Enough to explain what any of these five actors are doing together? Absolutely not.

That secrecy is doing most of the work at the moment because every possible detail suddenly feels like a clue. Is Lola playing Gracie’s friend, her enemy or someone who enters the story for ten minutes and ruins everyone’s life?

I would love to give you answers, but they genuinely gave us almost nothing to work with here.

For now, Please is simply the mysterious one in Lola’s schedule. We know Halina Reijn wrote it, A24 is producing and financing it, and the cast includes Gracie Abrams, Lola Tung, Tom Burke, Connor Storrie and David Jonsson. There is still no publicly confirmed release date.

We will probably be analysing the first photo the second they finally release it.

4. Ripe!

And then there is Ripe!, the project the internet is already being completely normal about (it is not).

Lola appeared in a teaser wearing a soccer uniform, sweaty from the game and staring down another female player on the field. That player is Rita Roca, who portrayed Gloria in the original short film and is returning opposite Lola for the new project. So far, Lola and Rita are the only cast members publicly connected to the feature.

The teaser was enough to connect Lola to a new version of Ripe!, a queer romance built around soccer, rivalry and two girls who may be feeling much more than competitive.

The original short film follows Sophie, an American exchange student in Spain, and Gloria, a local player who becomes both her rival and romantic interest. The two girls compete on the field while their relationship starts becoming increasingly personal off it.

The new project has not confirmed whether Lola is playing Sophie. We also do not have a wider cast list, a filming schedule, a distributor, a streaming platform or a release date. All we really have is the teaser, Lola sharing it herself and Rita returning as Gloria.

But honestly, the idea already makes sense for her. It is romantic without being soft all the time. The girls are attracted to each other, but they are also actively trying to beat each other. There is jealousy, physical tension and that horrible little problem of realising the person annoying you most might also be the person you cannot stop looking at.

Former professional soccer player Kelley O’Hara is involved as an executive producer, so hopefully the soccer will feel like a real part of the relationship instead of something the characters occasionally remember they are supposed to be playing.

I fear this one may cause problems when the full cast is finally announced.

So, What Are We Actually Getting?

At the moment, we have one horror movie in post production and expected in theatres during 2026, one dramedy that has already travelled through several festivals but is still waiting for a wider release, and two projects that are keeping their release plans hidden.

It is not the easiest schedule to follow, but the actual choices are really interesting. Lola is not making four versions of the same movie or playing the same girl with a different name.

Harper sounds funny and grounded. The Young People could make her terrifying. Please is keeping her completely unreadable, while Ripe! may give her a romantic role that feels competitive, physical and very different.

My guess is that The Young People will be the movie that surprises everyone, but Ripe! will be the one the internet refuses to behave normally about.

Either way, I’m happy we still cannot predict exactly what Lola will do next. It is much more fun watching someone build a career when they keep choosing roles we never thought to imagine for them.

posts.title: Dan Humphrey Was Never Gossip Girl in the Books
posts.subtitle: The novels gave Dan plenty to be guilty about. Secretly running Gossip Girl was never one of those things.
posts.body:
The television finale reveals Dan as Gossip Girl and explains the whole website as his extremely complicated way of getting Serena to notice him. He could not enter her world normally, so he spent six years publishing everyone’s secrets until the Upper East Side finally accepted his follow request.

Serena calls it a love letter. Five years later, she marries him. Everyone processes this information with the speed I personally associate with clicking “accept all cookies.”

But none of that happens in the books.

Dan is never Gossip Girl. Nobody else is revealed either. Gossip Girl stays anonymous because her identity is not a mystery the books are trying to solve. Her posts appear between chapters and work like small gossip roundups. She publishes sightings, responds to messages and discusses whichever relationship has become publicly embarrassing that week. The characters send her information, read what she writes and then become furious when the same system is used against them.

Very healthy system. No concerns.

Gossip Girl was written as the all knowing narrator. Basically, she is the book’s voice wearing better clothes and running a submissions inbox. She can follow Serena, Blair, Nate and Dan through completely separate parts of Manhattan because that is her job inside the story.

Book Dan has his own job, which is making every feeling he experiences much more exhausting than it needs to be. He lives on the Upper West Side with Rufus, Jenny and their cat, Marx. He attends Riverside Prep, smokes constantly, drinks absurd amounts of instant coffee and writes poems about death. If Dan speaks to Serena for four minutes, he can emotionally stretch that interaction across several chapters and possibly a first draft.

At the beginning of the novels, he is already obsessed with Serena despite barely knowing her. His real chance to get close to her arrives through Vanessa, who is making her own film version of War and Peace. Dan is cast as the male lead, Serena auditions opposite him and Vanessa immediately notices their chemistry because, unfortunately for her, she has eyes.

Later, while Blair holds the Kiss on the Lips party, Dan spends the evening with Serena and Vanessa at a performance by Vanessa’s sister. When Jenny calls because Chuck has cornered her at the party, Dan and Serena rush over to help. That is how Dan enters Serena’s life in the books.

He also remains a genuine outsider. Serena is interested in him for a while, but she does not revolve around him. When Dan feels left out, he is actually left out.

And Gossip Girl writes about him too. Dan is one of the people being watched, discussed and reduced to an initial whenever his love life becomes interesting enough. He is not deciding which version of himself the public gets to see.

To be clear, book Dan is not some misunderstood angel being unfairly blamed by television. The novels would never deprive us of his worst behaviour like that.

After footage involving Jenny and Nate circulates, Dan writes an angry poem called “Sluts.” Vanessa sends it to The New Yorker, where it gets published in a Valentine’s issue. The poem brings him professional attention, which is an insane reward for handling a family crisis in the most Dan Humphrey way possible. That moment tells us exactly what kind of writer he is in the books. Dan can be talented, judgmental and cruel, especially when he believes he has been embarrassed. He is fully capable of turning another person’s private life into material.

He just does it under his own name. His writing also creates real consequences. It affects Vanessa, complicates his relationships and gives other people the chance to judge him back. The books do not hide his worst decisions behind a second identity.

That is why making Dan Gossip Girl changes much more than the ending.

In the novels, gossip belongs to everyone. People submit tips when they want revenge, read the website when they are bored and complain about privacy when their own name appears. Gossip Girl has power because the entire group keeps supplying her with material. She is basically the worst group chat you have ever joined, except nobody can leave and the admin knows where you kissed Nate.

If the books revealed one person behind the website, everyone else could act like the problem had been found. Leaving Gossip Girl anonymous keeps the blame spread across the people who send, read and repeat everything she posts.

One of the show’s original writers later confirmed that Dan was not chosen from the beginning. The earlier scenes were not written to support that answer, which is why watching them again does not make the reveal smarter. It mostly makes Dan look like a man committed to privately acting surprised in front of kitchen appliances.

The books use Dan’s writing in a much simpler and better way. He writes poems because he is emotional, pretentious and desperate to be understood. Sometimes the poems are good. Sometimes they are cruel. Sometimes you want Vanessa to take away his coffee and wait for the mood to pass.

Television makes his writing the weapon he uses to enter Serena’s world. The books let it remain the reason Dan keeps complicating the life he already has.

milk mondays ruling:

Dan being Gossip Girl is an interesting idea until the rest of the story is required to support it. His motivation sounds believable. The actual timeline does not.

The books were right to leave Gossip Girl anonymous. She works better as the voice of a social circle that cannot stop exposing itself than as one boy’s six year plan for getting invited places.

The books let Gossip Girl watch everyone. Television made one character answer for the watching.

next on milk mondays:

Nate Was the Books’ Real Main Guy

The television series often treats Nate like an attractive notification that appears whenever a new woman joins the cast.

your ruling:

Did Gossip Girl need a face, or should Dan have been left alone with his poetry and several urgent reasons to calm down?

posts.title: Did Ned Actually Remember Peter at the End of Spider-Man: Brand New Day?
posts.subtitle: That handshake may be the first crack in Doctor Strange’s spell, but the movie leaves enough doubt to keep the answer open.
posts.body:
That handshake at the end may be the most important part of Peter Parker’s new beginning.

Warning: major spoilers for Spider Man: Brand New Day below.

Okay, we need to talk about that handshake.

Spider Man: Brand New Day spends most of its story making Peter live with the awful ending of No Way Home. Everyone still knows Spider Man exists, but nobody remembers Peter Parker. MJ does not remember loving him. Ned does not remember being his best friend. Peter remembers all of it.

Then, in the final scene, Ned completes their old best friend handshake without being taught it again.

That one movement makes Doctor Strange’s spell look much less complete.

First, what exactly does Ned remember before the ending?

Ned has not completely forgotten Spider Man.

Doctor Strange’s spell erased Peter Parker from people’s memories. It did not erase Spider Man. Ned can still remember that Spider Man saved him and MJ when they were younger. In Brand New Day, he is trying to work out who Spider Man is and has even built a Spidey Tracker to follow his appearances around New York.

The painful part is that Ned is searching for a superhero who once stood beside him every day, and he has no idea.

Peter eventually spends time with MJ and Ned again while wearing the Spider Man mask. For a little while, the three of them fall back into their old rhythm. Ned just does not know that the person behind the mask is the best friend missing from his memories.

MJ learns the truth first.

MJ knows what happened, but that is not the same as remembering it

MJ finds the letter Peter wrote for her, the one he planned to use to explain the life Doctor Strange’s spell erased.

She learns that she and Peter had a relationship. She learns about the spell. She understands that this stranger was once one of the most important people in her life.

But she does not suddenly remember loving him.

That difference is one of the smartest choices in the ending.

You can tell someone, “we were in love,” but you cannot hand them the feelings that once came with it. MJ makes that painfully clear to Peter. She knows something was taken from her, but the version of MJ standing in front of him cannot restart a relationship she has no memory of living through.

The Black Dahlia necklace keeps the door slightly open.

Near the end, MJ holds the broken necklace Peter gave her in Far From Home. It does not prove that her memories are returning, but the movie wants us to notice that a piece of their old relationship is still physically with her.

Now she knows who gave it to her too.

Whether the feelings attached to it can return is still unanswered.

Then Ned’s hands remember before his mind does

The final scene takes us back to the bodega.

Peter approaches Ned without his mask. Ned recognises him as the neighbour he met earlier, but nothing more. Then Peter begins their very specific handshake from Homecoming.

Ned follows every move.

Peter does not explain it. He does not teach him what comes next. Ned’s body already knows the pattern.

Only after they finish does Ned’s expression change.

He looks at Peter and says his name.

“Peter!”

Tiny scene. Huge problem for everyone who thought they finally understood Doctor Strange’s spell.

There is one detail that keeps the moment from being a complete confirmation. Earlier, MJ says Peter’s name around Ned while Peter is there as Spider Man. Ned has already heard that the superhero he is trying to identify may be called Peter.

So the final scene does not prove that every deleted memory came rushing back at once.

Ned may be connecting the clues. This neighbour is Peter. Peter is Spider Man. The handshake feels familiar before Ned understands why.

Or the handshake may be the first real crack in the spell.

The movie gives us enough evidence to argue both.

Is Doctor Strange’s spell breaking?

Right now, we do not know.

One theory is that Jean Grey’s telepathic powers affected the spell. Jean enters people’s minds throughout the movie, and her abilities become incredibly powerful during the final act. It makes sense that viewers have connected her presence to Ned’s sudden recognition.

But the movie never says Jean restored Ned’s memories. It does not show her trying to do it either.

For now, that remains a theory.

The stronger reading is that forgetting Peter and erasing every trace of his relationships are not exactly the same thing.

MJ can learn the facts without recovering the feelings she once had.

Ned can repeat a movement that belonged to his friendship with Peter without clearly remembering the years behind it.

That is far more interesting than everyone waking up one morning with their memories magically restored.

I hope the movie does not rush the answer

The saddest part of No Way Home was not only that MJ and Ned forgot Peter. It was that Peter chose to leave them alone after promising he would return and explain everything.

He saw them safe and happy, decided his life could put them in danger again and walked away carrying every memory by himself.

If one handshake instantly reverses all of that, his sacrifice becomes much smaller.

But if the ending begins a slower reconnection, I love it.

MJ does not owe Peter the relationship her old self had with him. Ned does not need every deleted memory returned in one magical download. Peter may have to earn a place in their lives again as the person he is now.

The old connection can still be there underneath it all.

That is why Ned’s handshake works so well as the final scene. The movie does not need him to explain what he remembers.

For a few seconds, his hands know Peter before we are sure his mind does.

Honestly, that hurts more than a neat answer would.

posts.title: 10 Hailey Bieber Outfits You Can Recreate on a Budget
posts.subtitle: From her oversized leather jackets to her tiny black dresses, these are the Hailey Bieber outfits that constantly go viral on TikTok and Instagram, recreated with affordable alternatives and shopping links.
posts.body:
Hailey Bieber’s wardrobe has become its own internet genre. Every few weeks, one of her outfits takes over Pinterest boards, TikTok moodboards, and Instagram saves.

We picked the 10 looks girls actually obsess over, then found budget friendly versions that give the same vibe without the Hailey Bieber bank account.

Quick note before we get into it: the “Pinterest save score” below is our editorial rating, not private Pinterest data. Shopping prices were checked on August 6, 2026, so sale prices and stock can change.

1. The Oversized Leather Jacket + Mini Shorts Look

This might be the purest form of Hailey Bieber street style: a massive leather jacket, almost invisible shorts, tiny sunglasses and heels.

In September 2025, she wore a Saint Laurent bubbled leather bomber in New York's West Village with a white cropped tee, tiny black shorts and Saint Laurent mules. The jacket alone was reported at $7,600, while the mules were $1,150. That means two pieces of the outfit already came to $8,750.

Paparazzi photo: https://www.marieclaire.com/fashion/celebrity-style/hailey-bieber-fall-jacket-trend-west-village/

Why girls are obsessed with it: The proportions do all the work. Huge jacket, tiny bottom, simple tee. It looks expensive without needing much underneath.

Key pieces: An oversized black faux leather jacket, tiny black shorts, fitted white tee, black kitten heels and oval sunglasses.

Budget recreation:

Black faux leather jacket, $19.94

Black pleated shorts, $7.34

White fitted ribbed tee, about $5.24

Black kitten heel mules, $10.49

Black oval sunglasses, $8.39

Budget total: $51.41

Original price reality: At least $8,750 for the confirmed jacket and shoes alone.

Budget tag: UNDER $52.51

Pinterest save score: 10/10

College girl friendly?: 7/10

Perfect for: Dinner, shopping, concerts and nights when you want your jacket to be the entire personality of the outfit.

Styling mistake to avoid: Don't wear a fitted leather jacket. The exaggerated size difference between the jacket and shorts is what creates the Hailey silhouette.

shop the look.

2. The “Model Off Duty” Airport Outfit

The original paparazzi version of this formula actually had matching tan joggers, not jeans. Hailey wore them with a hoodie, oversized Off White puffer, Acne Studios sneakers and sunglasses at JFK.

Photo: https://www.thezoereport.com/culture/hailey-baldwins-airport-style-is-comfort-done-right-its-so-easy-to-recreate-16811482

Her Acne Studios sneakers alone were listed at $380.

For a 2026 Hailey Bieber outfit inspo version, straight jeans make more sense. You still get the oversized top half proportions, but the outfit works for class, cafés and normal travel days too.

Key pieces: Oversized grey hoodie, relaxed straight jeans, clean sneakers and dark sunglasses.

Budget recreation:

Grey relaxed hoodie, $10.49

Relaxed blue jeans, $10.49

White trainers, $10.49

Black oval sunglasses, $8.39

Budget total: $39.87

Original price reality: The exact full airport total wasn't published, but the sneakers alone were $380.

Budget tag: UNDER $52.51

Pinterest save score: 8.5/10

College girl friendly?: 10/10

Perfect for: Flights, lectures, library days and long train rides.

Styling mistake to avoid: Skinny jeans completely change this outfit. Keep the denim loose and relaxed.

shop the look.

3. The Tiny Black Dress Everyone Saved

For a December 2021 trip to see The Nutcracker in London, Hailey wore a structured Acne Studios black mini with exaggerated shoulders, black Wolford tights and Saint Laurent pumps.

Photo: https://www.whowhatwear.com/hailey-baldwin-little-black-dress

The dress was listed at $580, with the Wolford tights around $55 before even adding the designer heels.

Why girls are obsessed: It proves a black mini doesn't need sequins, cut outs and twelve complicated straps. The shape is the statement.

Budget recreation:

Black ribbed bodycon mini, $7.34

Black semi sheer stockings, $8.19

Black pointed shoes, $10.49

Budget total: $26.02

Original price reality: At least $635 for the dress and tights, before Saint Laurent heels.

Budget tag: UNDER $52.51

Pinterest save score: 10/10

College girl friendly?: 6/10

Perfect for: Birthdays, winter dates, dinners and parties.

Styling mistake to avoid: Don't pile on jewellery. Black tights, clean heels and small earrings are enough.

shop the look.

4. The Oversized Blazer + Biker Shorts Combo

Long before biker shorts became everybody's errand uniform, Hailey was treating them like actual trousers.

One of the most copied versions came from Beverly Hills in December 2020: tiny black bike shorts, a grey sweatshirt, plaid oversized blazer and sneakers.

Paparazzi photo: https://www.harpersbazaar.com/celebrity/latest/a34884890/hailey-bieber-bike-shorts-plaid-blazer-photo/

Why it works: The tailored blazer stops the bike shorts from looking purely gym ish.

Budget recreation:

Oversized beige blazer, $10.49 on sale when checked

Black cycling shorts, $5.24

Grey hoodie, $10.49

White trainers, $10.49

Want the plaid closer to Hailey's? Try this grey checked option and size up.

Budget total: $36.71 with the beige blazer

Original price reality: A reliable exact total for Hailey's original outfit wasn't published.

Budget tag: UNDER $52.51

Pinterest save score: 9/10

College girl friendly?: 9/10

Perfect for: Coffee runs, campus, shopping and travel.

Styling mistake to avoid: Don't choose a blazer that stops exactly at your waist. You want it roomy and long enough to balance the bike shorts.

shop the look.

5. The Clean Girl Gym Outfit

In March 2026, Hailey stepped out in Los Angeles wearing black Alo layers with brown and cream SKYLRK sneakers.

Paparazzi photo: https://www.marieclaire.com/fashion/celebrity-style/black-leggings-brown-sneakers-outfit-hailey-bieber/

Her Alo Sway zip hoodie was $128 and the Softsculpt leggings were $144. That's $272 before the sneakers.

The formula: Black sports bra underneath, high waisted leggings, fitted zip up and simple trainers.

Budget recreation:

Black sports bra, $8.92

High waisted black leggings, $8.39

Black full sleeve zip jacket, $10.49

Grey running shoes, $10.49

Budget total: $38.29

Original price reality: $272 for the confirmed jacket and leggings before shoes.

Budget tag: UNDER $52.51

Pinterest save score: 9/10

College girl friendly?: 10/10

Perfect for: Pilates, gym days, airport mornings and the very important post workout iced coffee.

Styling mistake to avoid: Too many colours. The clean Hailey Bieber aesthetic works because the base stays almost monochrome.

shop the look.

6. The “Rich Girl Coffee Run” Outfit

This is less “I spent 20 minutes choosing my clothes” and more “I casually own a very good trench coat.”

For a January 2025 New York look, Hailey paired wide beige The Row trousers with a Magda Butrym trench, white tee, cardigan and loafers. It has exactly the rich girl coffee run energy we're after.

Photo: https://www.whowhatwear.com/fashion/celebrity-style/hailey-bieber-beige-trouser-trend

For an India friendly recreation, switch her tee for a basic tank.

Budget recreation:

Beige cropped trench, $20.99

White ribbed tank, $5.24

Beige linen blend wide leg trousers, $15.74

Budget total: $41.98

Original price reality: The exact full designer total wasn't publicly confirmed. Her original mixed Magda Butrym and The Row pieces, with a $150 cardigan also identified in the look.

Budget tag: UNDER $52.51

Pinterest save score: 9.5/10

College girl friendly?: 8/10

Perfect for: Brunch, internships, coffee dates, shopping and travel.

Styling mistake to avoid: Going too tight. The expensive looking part is the long, loose line created by the trench and wide trousers.

shop the look.

7. The Viral Date Night Look

This one is very 2026.

In July, Hailey wore a vintage Christian Dior by John Galliano red slip style mini in New York after Justin Bieber's World Cup performance. The vintage Dior dress was reported at $1,700.

Paparazzi photo: https://www.whowhatwear.com/fashion/celebrity-style/hailey-bieber-world-cup-after-party-vintage-dior-slip-dress-2026

The combination was simple: red mini, barely there black heels, little bag, tiny sunglasses.

Budget recreation:

Red lace sweetheart mini, $18.37

Black kitten heel mules, $10.49

Black top handle bag, $7.34

Oval sunglasses, $8.39

Budget total: $44.59

Original price reality: $1,700 for the Dior dress alone.

Budget tag: UNDER $52.51

Pinterest save score: 10/10

College girl friendly?: 5/10

Perfect for: Date night, birthdays and going out plans.

Styling mistake to avoid: Don't add a statement necklace, giant bag and chunky heels. The red dress already has the room.

shop the look.

8. The Baggy Jeans + Baby Tee Outfit

You probably already know the photo.

In January 2023, Hailey wore a tiny white X Karla “Nepo Baby” tee with loose vintage Levi's, chunky black Proenza Schouler shoes and a Prada bag.

Photo: https://www.vogue.com/article/hailey-bieber-nepo-baby-shirt

Forget the text on the original tee. The part of the outfit worth stealing is the proportion: miniature white top, huge blue jeans, substantial black shoes.

And it's still relevant. Hailey's 2026 Gap denim collaboration kept her relaxed '90s jeans obsession alive, with the Hailey Jeans priced at $89.95 and selling out quickly after release: https://www.marieclaire.com/fashion/celebrity-style/hailey-bieber-gap-jeans-review/

Budget recreation:

White fitted tee, about $5.24

Relaxed mid rise jeans, $10.49

Black penny loafers, $10.49

Core outfit: $15.73

Full budget total: $26.22 with shoes

Original price reality: An exact 2023 outfit total wasn't reliably published. It included vintage Levi's plus Prada and Proenza Schouler accessories.

Budget tags: CORE UNDER $21.00 / FULL LOOK UNDER $52.51

Pinterest save score: 10/10

College girl friendly?: 10/10

Perfect for: Literally campus.

Styling mistake to avoid: Buying jeans that are only slightly loose. This outfit needs proper baggy denim.

shop the look.

9. The All Black Street Style Look

Hailey's all black outfits are proof that “I'm wearing black” and “I styled an outfit” are not the same thing.

For a 2023 date night at Giorgio Baldi, she wore a boxy black trouser suit with a cropped black top, pointed heels, black shoulder bag, sunglasses and gold hoops.

Paparazzi photo: https://www.vogue.co.uk/news/article/hailey-bieber-trouser-suit

Why girls copy it: You don't need interesting colours when the proportions are good.

Budget recreation:

Black blazer, $27.29

Black wide leg trousers, $10.49 when checked

Black fitted tank, $5.24

Black pointed shoes, $10.49

Black bag, $7.34

Black sunglasses, $8.39

Budget total: $69.25

Original price reality: The exact original brands weren't fully identified. A luxury “shop the look” recreation published alongside the outfit came to £4,626 for just the blazer, trousers, tee and sunglasses, before shoes and bag.

Budget tag: UNDER $105.02

Pinterest save score: 9.5/10

College girl friendly?: 7/10

Perfect for: Dinners, presentations, internships and nights when colour feels like too much admin.

Styling mistake to avoid: Mixing six different complicated silhouettes. Keep the top fitted and let the blazer and trousers bring the volume.

shop the look.

10. The Vacation Outfit Pinterest Can't Stop Saving

Hailey's Cult Gaia Serita dress is basically ancient history by internet standards, yet the look is still floating around Pinterest vacation boards.

She wore the white and sand cut out knit maxi on vacation with Justin Bieber. Unlike most of this list, the famous image wasn't a paparazzi shot. Hailey posted the vacation photo herself.

Original photo/look page: https://www.vogue.com/article/hailey-bieber-summer-maxi-dress-cult-gaia

The Cult Gaia Serita has been listed around $458: https://cultgaia.com/products/serita-dress-sand

Why girls are still obsessed: It's the entire Hailey Bieber aesthetic on holiday. Neutral colour, skin showing in exactly the right places, uncomplicated accessories.

Budget recreation:

Off white backless halter maxi, $13.64

Ivory flat sandals, about $10.49

Black oval sunglasses, $8.39

Budget total: $32.52

Original price reality: Around $458 for the Cult Gaia dress alone.

Budget tag: UNDER $52.51

Pinterest save score: 10/10

College girl friendly?: 6/10 normally, 10/10 on the Goa trip

Perfect for: Beach holidays, resort dinners, honeymoons and poolside plans.

Styling mistake to avoid: Heavy jewellery and formal heels. This look only works if it still feels like you got dressed for vacation in five minutes.

shop the look.

The Last Sip

The funny thing about Hailey Bieber outfit inspo is that the expensive part usually isn't what makes you save the photo.

It's the proportions.

The giant leather jacket with tiny shorts. The baby tee with huge jeans. The fitted gym set under a zip up. The enormous blazer over biker shorts. The tiny red dress with almost nothing competing with it.

And once you spot that pattern, recreating the Hailey Bieber aesthetic becomes much easier.

You don't need the $7,600 jacket.

You need the silhouette.

posts.title: Spider Man’s Producer Warned Tom Holland and Zendaya Not to Date
posts.subtitle: Amy Pascal gave the same warning to three generations of Spider Man couples. Tom and Zendaya ignored it and turned the pattern into a marriage.
posts.body: Before Spider Man: Homecoming even gave us Peter and MJ, producer Amy Pascal had one warning for Tom Holland and Zendaya: please do not date each other. When they were first cast, Pascal pulled them aside separately and told them, “Don’t go there. Just don’t. Try not to.” And honestly, she had reasons. Tobey Maguire and Kirsten Dunst had already fallen for each other while making the first Spider Man. They dated for about a year, then broke up before Spider Man 2. Director Sam Raimi later admitted he worried about whether they would still have the same chemistry on screen. Thankfully they did, because losing Peter and MJ chemistry over an ex situation would have been painful for everyone involved. Then it happened again. Andrew Garfield met Emma Stone while filming The Amazing Spider Man. They played Peter Parker and Gwen Stacy, fell in love in real life and were together for around four years. Pascal later said she had given Andrew and Emma the same dating warning. Nobody listened to Amy Pascal. Not once. So when Tom and Zendaya came along, she knew this story a little too well. Rumours about them started around Homecoming in 2017, but they kept their relationship private. Then, in 2021, they were photographed kissing in a car and the secret was over. Except this Spider Man love story ended differently. Tom and Zendaya got engaged, married in private and have now made four Spider Man movies together. Their marriage was confirmed in 2026. And the sweetest part might actually be what happened while making Spider Man: Brand New Day. Tom recently explained that while filming a scene with Zendaya, something did not feel right. He asked her if she felt it too. She did. They spoke to the filmmakers, everyone agreed, and the scene was rewritten and reshot. Which is kind of funny considering the whole reason Pascal warned them about dating was that relationships could complicate the work. Ten years later, their relationship is actually improving the work. Tobey and Kirsten happened. Andrew and Emma happened. Amy gave the warning again anyway. And Tom and Zendaya turned the Spider Man dating curse into a marriage.

posts.title: The 2016 Fashion Comeback Brought the Gossip Girl Fantasy Back With It
posts.subtitle: 2026 started by reviving chokers, skinny jeans and Tumblr-era fashion, then moved into statement coats, prep, layers and accessories that feel very familiar to anyone who grew up watching Blair and Serena.
posts.body: The funniest thing about 2026’s obsession with 2016 is that one of the clearest fashion references it now resembles was not even around in 2016. Gossip Girl ended in 2012. Still, look at what people are excited about wearing again right now: statement coats, preppy pieces, layers, tights, loafers, hair accessories and outfits with a lot more going on than a plain top and jeans. Put those pieces together and the result starts feeling less like an exact recreation of 2016 and much more like the kind of wardrobe Blair Waldorf would have taken very seriously. The 2016 nostalgia itself is huge. At the beginning of this year, searches for “2016” on TikTok rose by more than 450%, while searches for “2016 makeup” went up 600%. People started bringing back old filters, songs, makeup, chokers and skinny jeans. Fashion followed the same pattern. Skinny jeans, bomber jackets, lace slip dresses, backless loafers, ankle boots and skinny scarves have all been discussed as 2016 pieces returning in 2026. Even the styling has changed just enough to make the old clothes feel current, with fitted jeans being worn with oversized coats and loafers instead of recreating an entire 2016 outfit. But this is where the “2016” label starts getting a little loose. The fashion people are wearing and saving in 2026 has moved beyond pieces that actually belonged to that year. Preppy clothes are back. Checks are back. Layering is becoming interesting again. Brooches and noticeable accessories are showing up again. Oversized outerwear is everywhere. Headbands are having another moment too. None of these things belong to one year, but together they bring back a style of dressing that Gossip Girl was very good at: you could look at an outfit and immediately understand the person wearing it. Blair is the easiest example. Her clothes were extremely specific. She had headbands, coloured and textured tights, fitted coats, skirts, collars, bows, pearls and bags that all looked chosen to belong together. Serena dressed very differently, with taller boots, shorter dresses, looser layers, sequins and clothes that looked less planned, even when they clearly were. Jenny eventually built an entirely different wardrobe. Chuck could walk into a room in a purple suit and make the rest of the Upper East Side look underdressed. [IMAGE2:right:medium] The clothes were doing actual character work, which is why copying one Blair outfit can still make someone look recognisably “Blair” before you even mention Gossip Girl. Eric Daman, the costume designer behind the show, has talked about how important tights and coats were for defining personal style. He also wanted girls watching the show who could never buy the expensive clothes on screen to feel that they could still take part in the fashion. That detail matters because the Gossip Girl fantasy was never limited to owning exactly what Blair owned. You could take the idea instead. Add interesting tights to a skirt. Put a dramatic coat over a normal outfit. Wear the headband. Choose the bag that makes the whole thing make sense. The characters gave people a formula they could recreate at completely different budgets. Tumblr did a similar thing a few years later. A saved photo of a coat, a pair of boots, a messy bedroom, a lipstick colour and a song could all become one aesthetic. People were building entire versions of themselves out of images they liked. That is why the current nostalgia makes more sense when you stop treating “2016” like a strict twelve-month fashion archive. People remember eras through feelings and visuals, and those memories get mixed together. 2009 Blair Waldorf, early-2010s Tumblr, 2016 chokers and a 2026 oversized coat can easily end up on the same moodboard because they are giving someone the same thing they came looking for: a reason to have fun with how they look. There is also a big difference between bringing a trend back and dressing exactly as people did ten years ago. The current 2016 revival is already changing the old pieces. A skinny jean can now be balanced with a much bigger coat. A slip dress can sit under a structured blazer. Current styling is mixing the older pieces with 2026 proportions, which makes the comeback much easier to wear if you have no interest in looking like your old camera roll. And this is where the Gossip Girl connection becomes useful rather than just nostalgic. Blair and Serena rarely dressed around one trend. Their outfits worked because several pieces created one clear look. That may also explain why people are reacting so strongly to this particular comeback. For the last few years, a lot of online fashion has been organised into very clean formulas where the goal is to match one recognisable aesthetic. Gossip Girl came from a different kind of fashion fantasy. Blair could wear a patterned coat, coloured tights, a headband, a dress and jewellery in the same outfit. Serena could pile a jacket, scarf, boots, necklaces and a huge bag together. [IMAGE3:left:medium] It gave people permission to care about the whole outfit again, including the slightly unnecessary accessory that serves absolutely no practical purpose but makes everything better. The interesting part of the 2016 revival is where it goes next. Fashion nostalgia rarely stays inside the exact year printed on the label. Once people decide they miss an era, they start pulling in the clothes, shows, music and internet aesthetics surrounding it too. That is already happening here.
